assessments.reasoning: I independently retrieved and verified the exact bytes of System Programming in a High Level Language and inspected the cited passage (A §§1.4 and 2.1, printed pp. 5 and 7–8 (physical PDF pp. 9, 11–12)). Section 1.4 says the work was based on the existing Algol68 language and concentrated on implementation. Section 2.1 describes the new 1972 portable Algol68C compiler and notes the predecessor’s subset and extensions.

challenge.method: Compare the choice of base language against Z70’s earlier two-type language, omissions and extensions, and the distinct compiler choice on printed page 8.
challenge.results: Z70 was a predecessor language and compiling system. The portable Cambridge project is the named implementation. Its documented differences fit the frozen narrower relation.

limitations: The relationship uses the compiler as the target and is limited to the Cambridge project as Birrell describes it.
